annotation_schema.description: Each case maps to domain-specific conceptual failure reasons for ToGMAL similarity-based retrieval

fields.domain_specific_why: Why this domain causes this failure
fields.similar_tasks_will_fail: Other tasks with same conceptual profile

cases.task_description: Regular pentagon area after folding vertices to center
conceptual_requirements: Golden ratio φ = (1+√5)/2 in pentagon geometry

what_model_knows: Pentagon folding creates smaller similar pentagon ✓
conceptual_understanding.understanding_level: Complete - model grasps all geometric concepts

execution_failure_point.what_happened: Gets 2 - 2√5 but then claims this equals √5 - 1

domain_specific_why.reason: Irrational number algebra requires careful tracking of √5 terms
domain_specific_why.why_geometry_specific: Pentagon geometry inherently involves φ and √5 - not simple rational numbers
domain_specific_why.computational_challenge: Cannot verify (a + b√5)(c + d√5) expansions reliably
domain_specific_why.when_this_matters: Any geometry with golden ratio (pentagons, pentagrams, icosahedrons)

failure_mechanism.pattern: Pattern 6: Makes error in polynomial/radical expansion, doesn't verify by substitution
failure_mechanism.guessing_behavior: Gets nonsense result, guesses answer from choices

similar_tasks_will_fail: Any algebraic manipulation with nested radicals (√(a+b√c))

cases.task_description: Minimum operations to remove adjacent almost-equal characters

execution_failure_point.correct_logic: Should only check word[i] vs word[i-1] (adjacent only)

domain_specific_why.reason: Confusion between DP index relationships and problem adjacency constraint
domain_specific_why.why_dp_specific: DP naturally considers previous states (i-1, i-2, ...) but problem constraint is about string adjacency, not DP index adjacency
domain_specific_why.conceptual_conflation: Mixes 'DP lookback' (i-2 is relevant for DP) with 'problem constraint' (only i-1 is adjacent in string)
domain_specific_why.when_this_matters: Any DP where problem constraint differs from DP index relationships
domain_specific_why.root_cause: Problem space (string adjacency) ≠ solution space (DP index)

failure_mechanism.pattern: Pattern 2: Understands core, but adds unnecessary complexity that creates bugs
failure_mechanism.why_no_recovery: Code looks reasonable, extra check seems 'defensive'
failure_mechanism.subtlety: i-2 is relevant for DP state, just not for this problem's constraint

similar_tasks_will_fail: DP on sequences where constraint is local (k-window) but DP considers broader history
Stock trading with cooldown (1-day cooldown ≠ i-1 state dependency)
House robber with specific spacing constraints
String matching where pattern constraint differs from DP recurrence structure
Any problem where 'previous step in DP' ≠ 'relevant constraint scope'

cases.task_description: 3 people, 4 attributes each, 7 constraints - find avocado's position
conceptual_requirements: Process ordering constraints (A left of B)

what_model_knows: Constraints imply ordering: cranberry < tram < avocado ✓

execution_failure_point.what_happened: Correctly deduces avocado at position 3, but answers '2'
execution_failure_point.error_type: Variable reference confusion - answers with tram's position instead

domain_specific_why.reason: Multiple variables (cranberry, tram, avocado) bound to positions - reports wrong variable
domain_specific_why.why_csp_specific: CSPs have many variable bindings in working memory (person1→{tram, cranberry, ...}, person2→{...}, person3→{avocado, ...})
domain_specific_why.cognitive_load: Tracks 3 people × 4 attributes = 12 variable bindings simultaneously
domain_specific_why.when_this_matters: When question asks 'where is X?' but model just reasoned about Y's position
domain_specific_why.root_cause: Variable retrieval from working memory fails - gets 'position just mentioned' not 'position of queried item'

failure_mechanism.pattern: Pattern 3: Correct reasoning, but substitutes wrong variable at retrieval
failure_mechanism.why_no_recovery: Model doesn't re-check 'question asks for avocado, I'm answering with position 2, does avocado have position 2?'
failure_mechanism.recency_bias: Likely answers with most recently mentioned position (tram's)

similar_tasks_will_fail: Scheduling: 'Which day does Alice work?' when just reasoned about Bob's schedule
Network routing: 'Which port for service X?' when just computed Y's port
Database query: Multiple JOINs, SELECT asks for column from table A, returns column from table B
Any multi-variable binding where final question requires lookup
Configuration problems with many attribute assignments

cases.task_description: Euler's method for dy/dx = 3x + 4y, h=0.25, find y(1)

what_model_knows: Euler's method: y_{n+1} = y_n + h·f(x_n, y_n) ✓

execution_failure_point.error_type: Basic arithmetic failures in multi-step computation

domain_specific_why.reason: Numerical methods require exact arithmetic across many iterations - errors compound
domain_specific_why.why_numerical_methods_specific: Each step feeds into next step, so errors propagate exponentially in iterative algorithms
domain_specific_why.arithmetic_chain: Step 1 error → affects step 2 → affects step 3 → affects step 4
domain_specific_why.when_this_matters: Any iterative numerical algorithm (Newton's method, Runge-Kutta, finite differences, gradient descent)
domain_specific_why.shocking_finding: BOTH SOTA models made arithmetic errors - winner just had SMALLER errors

failure_mechanism.pattern: Pattern 4: Basic arithmetic fails (addition, multiplication), errors cascade through iterations
failure_mechanism.why_no_recovery: Doesn't verify by substituting final y(1) back into original ODE

similar_tasks_will_fail: Monte Carlo simulations with iterative updates
Compound interest calculations over multiple periods
Any algorithm where y_{n+1} = f(y_n) and need 5+ iterations

cases.task_description: 20+ people at locations, each tells truth or lies. Given statements, deduce who's truthful.

what_model_knows: If A says 'B lies' and A is truthful, then B lies ✓
Some facts are given (Tala tells truth) ✓
Can deduce Quan lies from Tala's truthfulness ✓

execution_failure_point.what_happened: Deduces Jaxon lies, Hiroshi tells truth, Anika tells truth
execution_failure_point.correct_answer: Jaxon tells truth, Hiroshi lies, Anika lies (exactly backwards!)
execution_failure_point.error_type: Never verified conclusion against established facts

domain_specific_why.reason: Boolean SAT problems require checking assignments satisfy ALL constraints
domain_specific_why.why_logic_specific: In logic puzzles, you deduce implications but must verify final assignment is consistent with all given facts
domain_specific_why.missing_step: Should check: 'If Jaxon lies, then his statement about Quan must be false. Jaxon said Quan lies. Quan DOES lie. Contradiction!'
domain_specific_why.when_this_matters: Any constraint satisfaction where you generate candidates but must validate
domain_specific_why.root_cause: No verification phase - generates answer, doesn't backtrack when inconsistent
domain_specific_why.cognitive_gap: Forward chaining (implications) works, backward verification missing

failure_mechanism.pattern: Pattern 5: Performs deduction, arrives at conclusion, never verifies against known facts

similar_tasks_will_fail: SAT/CSP solving (generate assignment, must verify constraints)
Graph coloring (assign colors, must verify no adjacent same color)
Scheduling constraints (assign times, must verify all constraints met)
Type inference (assign types, must verify consistency)
Any problem where solution is 'proposed assignment' that must satisfy multiple constraints

cases.task_description: Count sequences of increasing subsets, compute K mod 10

conceptual_understanding.response_a: Wrong formula (thinks n choices per element, forgets 'not included' option) but arithmetic correct
conceptual_understanding.response_b: Correct formula (n+1 choices per element) but arithmetic wrong
conceptual_understanding.understanding_level: Mixed - one understands concept, other executes correctly

execution_failure_point.what_happened: Response B claims 10^10 mod 10 = 5 (completely wrong! should be 0)
execution_failure_point.shocking: Response A: wrong concept + correct arithmetic → WINS

domain_specific_why.reason: Combinatorics requires both setup AND computation - failure in either means wrong answer
domain_specific_why.why_combinatorics_specific: Counting problems have two phases: (1) identify formula, (2) compute value. Phase 2 can dominate outcome.
domain_specific_why.arithmetic_dominance: In this case, arithmetic accuracy mattered MORE than conceptual understanding
domain_specific_why.when_this_matters: Probability calculations, expected values, counting problems with large numbers
domain_specific_why.root_cause: Even trivial modular arithmetic (10^k mod 10 = 0) fails
domain_specific_why.implication: Correct reasoning doesn't guarantee correct answer if arithmetic fails

failure_mechanism.mechanism: Arithmetic errors compound + guessing when stuck
failure_mechanism.pattern: Pattern 4: Basic arithmetic failures. Pattern 1: Gives up and guesses
failure_mechanism.why_no_recovery: Response B gets 0, sees it doesn't match choices, gives up and guesses B
failure_mechanism.counter_intuitive: Better understanding can LOSE to worse understanding with better arithmetic

similar_tasks_will_fail: Probability of compound events (multiplication of many small probabilities)
Modular arithmetic in cryptography (a^b mod m)
Any counting problem requiring exact numerical answer

execution_failure_point.consequence: Gets y² = -1/4 → 'imaginary roots' → misses y = -1/2 solutions

domain_specific_why.reason: Polynomial factorization requires synthetic division or algebraic manipulation - error-prone for models
domain_specific_why.why_algebra_specific: Factoring (ax³ + bx² + cx + d) / (x - r) → (x - r)(ax² + bx + c) requires careful coefficient matching
domain_specific_why.missing_verification: Should expand (y - 1/2)(-8y² - 2) back and see it doesn't equal original
domain_specific_why.when_this_matters: Solving higher-order polynomials, partial fraction decomposition, algebraic simplification
domain_specific_why.root_cause: Can't perform polynomial long division reliably
domain_specific_why.propagation: Wrong factorization → wrong quadratic → wrong roots → misses half the solutions

failure_mechanism.pattern: Pattern 6: Makes error in factorization, doesn't verify by expanding
failure_mechanism.why_no_recovery: Accepts 'imaginary roots' conclusion without questioning why cubic over reals would have complex roots
failure_mechanism.severity: Misses 50% of solutions (2 out of 4 angles)

similar_tasks_will_fail: Any algebraic manipulation with multiple steps

cases.task_description: Maximize tastiness eating courses, two states (healthy/upset), don't die
conceptual_requirements: State transition logic (antidotal → changes state, poisonous → changes state)

execution_failure_point.what_happened: Updates dp_upset[i] when should update dp_healthy[i]
execution_failure_point.error_type: State confusion - which state to update

domain_specific_why.reason: DP state transitions require tracking 'from state X, action A, go to state Y' - confuses source and target
domain_specific_why.why_dp_specific: DP maintains multiple state arrays. Transition 'upset + antidotal → healthy' means update dp_healthy, not dp_upset
domain_specific_why.cognitive_load: Two state arrays (dp_healthy, dp_upset) in working memory, easy to confuse which to update
domain_specific_why.when_this_matters: Any DP with 2+ states (stock buy/sell, game states, network states)
domain_specific_why.root_cause: Similar to variable confusion (Pattern 3) but in DP context
domain_specific_why.subtlety: Logic 'if upset, eat antidotal → become healthy' is clear, but translating to 'update dp_healthy[i]' fails

failure_mechanism.pattern: Pattern 3: Right logic, wrong target variable
failure_mechanism.why_no_recovery: Code compiles, logic sounds reasonable on surface
failure_mechanism.severity: Wrong state updated → wrong answer on test cases

similar_tasks_will_fail: String DP with multiple states (match/insert/delete in edit distance)
Any DP where dp[state1][i] vs dp[state2][i] matters

cases.task_description: What is Baumol-Tobin money holdings formula?
conceptual_requirements: Understand transaction costs, interest rate, bonds

conceptual_understanding.response_b: Recalls M = √(2bZ / i) - factor of 2 in WRONG place ✗
conceptual_understanding.qualitative_understanding: Both understand M increases with b,Z and decreases with i ✓
conceptual_understanding.understanding_level: Qualitative understanding perfect, quantitative precision inconsistent

execution_failure_point.what_happened: Factor of 2 appears in numerator instead of denominator

domain_specific_why.reason: Economic models have precise formulas with constants - misremembering placement changes result
domain_specific_why.why_economics_specific: Baumol-Tobin derivation from optimization gives specific √(bZ/2i). Factor of 2 from FOC of cost minimization.
domain_specific_why.qualitative_vs_quantitative: Qualitative relationships (↑b → ↑M) are robust, quantitative constants (factor of 2) are fragile
domain_specific_why.when_this_matters: Black-Scholes (exact σ√T term), CAPM (β coefficient), Solow growth (saving rate s)
domain_specific_why.root_cause: Factual recall from training data - stochastic retrieval
domain_specific_why.stochasticity: SAME model (Claude-3.5) gets it right in one response, wrong in another

failure_mechanism.pattern: Pattern 7: Knows concept/model name, gets constants/factors wrong
failure_mechanism.why_no_recovery: Doesn't verify by deriving from first principles or checking textbook
failure_mechanism.severity: 10-20% of formula recalls may have wrong constant placement

similar_tasks_will_fail: Any finance/economics formula with specific constants
Statistical formulas (n-1 vs n in variance)

retrieval_flow: 2. ToGMAL computes similarity to these 9 annotated cases
5. Return contextualized risk: 'This task is similar to Case 4 (Euler's method). LLMs fail because: iterative arithmetic compounds errors over 5+ steps. Risk multiplier: 3.5x'

risk_aggregation.if_multiple_neighbors_match: Take max(risk_multiplier) or average weighted by similarity

confidence_levels.very_high: Both models failed directly on this pattern
confidence_levels.high: One model failed directly, mechanism clear

summary_for_togmal.key_insight: Each annotation provides DOMAIN-SPECIFIC WHY, not just generic pattern. ToGMAL can say 'Fails because pentagon geometry involves golden ratio and algebraic manipulation of √5' not just 'fails at algebra'.
